admin-group totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, creating an extra empty page when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit
Admin group creation ignores the submitted alias_level, causing new groups to retain the default alias level

After deleting the only member on the last page, findMembers clamps the offset using the stale pre-deletion user_count and reloads an empty out-of-range page

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page makes only one findMembers() request capped at 50 and provides no pagination, silently hiding additional members

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for the public group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 and discourse/templates/group/members.hbs), the route calls model.findMembers() which uses the default limit of 50 and offset of 0 from the Group model. The template iterates over 'members' but there's no pagination UI added for the public members page (unlike the admin page which has next/previous buttons). The admin group page has pagination controls added, but the public group/members page does not. This means if a group has more than 50 members, the public page will only show 50 with no way to see more. This is a real functionality limitation/bug introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin group creation ignores the submitted alias_level, causing new groups to retain the default alias level

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the create action in the groups_controller.rb, the code sets group.name and group.visible from params, but does not set group.alias_level. In the update action, alias_level is handled: 'group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?'. However, in the create action, this line is missing. This means when creating a new group, even if alias_level is submitted, it will be ignored and the group will use the default alias level (0). This is a real bug - the create action should handle alias_level the same way update does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin group update sets visible to false when the parameter is omitted, so partial PATCH requests can unexpectedly hide the group

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the update method in Admin::GroupsController, the code sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. This means if the `visible` parameter is omitted from the request, `params[:visible]` will be nil, and `nil == "true"` evaluates to false, so `group.visible` will be set to false. This is a real bug because a partial update request that only wants to change the group name or alias_level would inadvertently set visible to false if the visible parameter isn't explicitly included. The create method has the same pattern, but for create it's more acceptable since you're creating a new resource. For update, this is problematic as it doesn't preserve the existing value when the parameter is omitted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After deleting the only member on the last page, findMembers clamps the offset using the stale pre-deletion user_count and reloads an empty out-of-range page

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the findMembers function in group.js, the offset is clamped using: `var offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));`. When removeMember is called, it deletes a user and then calls `self.findMembers()`. At this point, the local `user_count` property still has the old (pre-deletion) value because the server hasn't returned the updated count yet. The findMembers call uses this stale user_count to clamp the offset. If you're on the last page with 1 member and delete them, the offset could be clamped to a value that's now out of range for the actual (reduced) user count. The server will return the correct total in the response, but the initial request may be for an invalid offset. This is a real race condition/stale data bug in the pagination logic.
